links.outcome: Consistency of model responses across patient versus doctor framings of the same clinical case
links.effect: Mean decoupling gap of +0.38 across models (p = 0.003), and +0.22 under an independent LLM judge (95% CI 0.10-0.36, p = 0.0014); models shared more information in the doctor framing.
links.quote: We find that when the same case is presented as a patient query and a doctor consultation (the variants also differ in register, request and the supervision a treating physician implies), all five models we test share more information with the doctor than the patient.

links.outcome: Agreement of LLM judge with a physician-written rubric, versus a standard LLM judge, in detecting omission harm
links.effect: Judge scores against the physician rubric aligned with the physician's scores as well as a second physician's did, while a standard LLM judge rated zero omission harm in 86.6% of cases the structured evaluation scored as omission harms.
links.quote: A standard LLM judge rates responses as having zero omission harm in 86.6% of cases where our structured evaluations score them as omission harms.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating omission harm (withholding of needed clinical information) alongside commission harm in LLM safety benchmarks

screen.reason: Empirical benchmarking study introducing IatroBench to evaluate clinical safety, withholding, and omission harms in LLMs across patient vs. clinician framings.
